issues.claim: Calling `Remove` on an entity in the `Added` state moves it to `Detached`, not to `Deleted`.
issues.problem: The fact matches the DbSet.Remove API remarks: an entity in Added is detached, not marked Deleted. The fetched excerpts of the two cited pages do not show it, and the Change Tracking overview excerpt has nothing on Remove. The generator also flagged it as unverified. The same gap applies to the cited support for options b, d and g (Attach and Update with set or unset keys, Remove on an untracked entity). The excerpt supports only f (deleted entities detached after SaveChanges) and the claim that Remove marks the blog Deleted.
issues.suggestedFix: Add the API reference page for DbSet<TEntity>.Remove (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.entityframeworkcore.dbset-1.remove) as a link, with a linkTitle in both locales, and cite it for option a. Alternatively confirm the exact wording on the explicit-tracking page.

issues.claim: The EF Core documentation warns explicitly: SQL Server does not allow composing over stored procedure calls, and any additional operators on top of such a call produce invalid SQL.
issues.problem: I recall this warning on the SQL Queries page. The fetched excerpt stops at 'Composable SQL queries generally begin with the SELECT', so it does not show it, and the sandbox cannot run it. The excerpt only shows that EF Core treats the SQL as a subquery, which supports the first half of option b. The claim that EXEC fails, and how, is unconfirmed from the item. In practice EF Core usually throws InvalidOperationException about non-composable SQL (suggesting AsEnumerable) before SQL is sent.
issues.suggestedFix: Confirm the warning and the AsEnumerable/AsAsyncEnumerable advice on the sql-queries page, or soften the wording to 'the documentation says composable SQL must begin with SELECT, and EF Core throws a run-time exception (typically InvalidOperationException saying the SQL is non-composable)'.
